Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

AudiomothR 0.4.1 (in preparation)

Changes after the review of Julia Guerra Carande (rOpenSci reviewer template).

  • read_audiomoth() notes, once per session, when the results folder is in the temporary folder of R (tempdir(), as in the examples and the vignettes): it is deleted when R closes.
  • create_validation() warns, on Linux, when the page is in /tmp and Firefox or Chromium are installed as snaps (Ubuntu): they cannot open files there.
  • spectrogram_image() and spectrogram_video() say where they saved the file.
  • Validation page: a click on a spectrogram shows it at full size (a click or Esc closes it), while the page keeps its compact layout.
  • check_requirements() shows the version of Quarto and says when it is older than 1.4 (before, an old Quarto was reported as not found), and loads knitr and rmarkdown instead of only looking for them: an old package that they use (often htmltools) prevents loading them, and the message says which one to update.
  • Messages that quote an error of another program or package no longer show its braces doubled ({{x}}).
  • Vignette 1: a table of the thresholds of the workflow (min_confidence of each step, example_confidence, location_threshold…), what each one decides, and why a window with two species is not necessarily wrong.
  • README: who the package is for; installation with the vignettes and what it needs (pandoc); old Quarto and packages that do not load in the usual problems.
  • The examples of create_report() and gbif_species_list() can now be run (example(create_report)): they use the example card and a temporary folder. Those of setup_birdnet(), analyze_birdnet() and process_audiomoth() are still not run, because they install BirdNET (about 3 GB).
  • Contribution guidelines (.github/CONTRIBUTING.md), a code of conduct (Contributor Covenant 2.1) and templates for the issues, linked from the README.
  • Web site of the package, built with pkgdown: https://ajcanepa.github.io/AudiomothR/. The vignettes can be read there without building them when installing.
  • Vignette 1 and the README: where to find the files, and the validation page that does not open in Firefox on Ubuntu, in the usual problems.

AudiomothR 0.4.0

New features

  • Copy of the card (copy_to in read_audiomoth() and process_audiomoth()): the card is first copied to the disk and everything is done with the copy, so the card can be formatted for the next deployment, the recordings are kept as a backup, and the examples, the validation page and new analyses keep working without the card. copy_to = TRUE copies it into <output>/recordings/<first date>-<last date>/; a folder copies it into <folder>/AudioMoth_<ID>/<first date>-<last date>/. The copy keeps the structure and the dates of the card, checks the size of each file and continues where it stopped. The original folder is kept in the new column card_folder of AudioMoth_<ID>_deployments.csv.
  • Own list of species (species_list in analyze_birdnet(), also through process_audiomoth()): only the species of the list are analysed, instead of those expected by the location filter. The list may be a vector of scientific names, the species list of BirdNET-Analyzer (.txt), a CSV file with a column of scientific names or a data frame; names of BirdNET, the IOC World Bird List, Observation.org or GBIF are accepted. read_species_list() reads and checks a list, and the package includes a template (inst/extdata/example/species_list.csv). Each list is a different analysis in the cache, which keeps the list used (species_list.csv). The report states which filter was used.
  • gbif_species_list(): the bird species observed within a radius of the recorder, in the months of its recordings, in the datasets of eBird, Observation.org and iNaturalist published by GBIF (public API, without an account or a key), translated into BirdNET names and ready to be used as species_list. Useful for species that the location filter of BirdNET leaves out (nocturnal, secretive or scarce species, little visited areas). A new table (inst/extdata/taxonomy/birdnet_v2.4_to_gbif.csv.gz, built with data-raw/build_gbif_keys.R) links each bird of BirdNET v2.4 to its species in the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy.

Documentation

  • The help of analyze_birdnet(), the vignette and the README explain how the location filter works (BirdNET metadata model trained with eBird checklists, probability of occurrence per site and week, threshold 0.03), when it may leave out species that are present, and the alternatives (lower threshold, own list, list from GBIF, no filter).
  • The vignette and the README recommend copying the card before working.
  • The vignette is now split into three, to be read in order: 1. Getting started: the complete workflow (vignette("audiomothr-1-workflow"), every step and every function with the example card, with images of the validation page and of the report, checks and a section of usual problems), 2. Which species BirdNET looks for (vignette("audiomothr-2-species")) and 3. Several cards, several boxes and reports (vignette("audiomothr-3-boxes")).
  • New example data: inst/extdata/example/gbif_species_list.csv, the list of the species observed in GBIF around the example site.

Other changes

  • jsonlite is a new dependency (already installed with reticulate).
  • Julia Guerra Carande joins the authors. The ORCID of the authors is now in DESCRIPTION and CITATION.cff, with their affiliations.

AudiomothR 0.3.0

Breaking changes

  • The package is now in English: functions, arguments, messages, help, the vignette, the PDF report and the columns and names of the result files. Equivalences with version 0.2.0:

    0.2.0 0.3.0
    leer_audiomoth(carpeta, coordenadas, punto, precision_m, zona_horaria, salida) read_audiomoth(folder, coordinates, site, precision_m, time_zone, output)
    leer_config() read_config()
    parsear_coordenadas() parse_coordinates()
    seleccionar_carpeta() choose_folder()
    preparar_audios() prepare_audio()
    analizar_birdnet(confianza_minima, idioma, filtro_ubicacion, umbral_ubicacion, solapamiento, sensibilidad, hilos, reanalizar) analyze_birdnet(min_confidence, language, location_filter, location_threshold, overlap, sensitivity, threads, reanalyze)
    leer_detecciones() read_detections()
    resumen_especies() species_summary()
    especies_detectadas(confianza_ejemplos) detected_species(example_confidence)
    seleccionar_ejemplos() select_examples()
    extraer_ejemplos(margen_s, estilo = "desplazamiento") extract_examples(margin_s, style = "scroll")
    imagen_espectrograma(), video_espectrograma() spectrogram_image(), spectrogram_video()
    exportar_observation(min_detecciones, solo_sin_dudas, desde, hasta, equivalencias, archivo) export_observation(min_detections, no_doubts_only, from, to, equivalences, file)
    crear_informe(cajas, por_caja, salida, titulo, abrir) create_report(recorders, by_recorder, output, title, open)
    procesar_audiomoth(especies_ejemplo, n_ejemplos, confianza_ejemplos, estilo_video, informe) process_audiomoth(example_species, n_examples, example_confidence, video_style, report)
    comprobar_requisitos() check_requirements()

    Results files: AudioMoth_<ID>_recordings.csv, _detections.csv, _observation.csv, examples/, report/ and validation/. Results of version 0.2.0 must be produced again (the BirdNET cache has a new layout).

  • The language of the common names is taken from the operating system (language in analyze_birdnet()); notes of Observation.org are in English unless the language is Spanish.

  • The minimum confidence is inclusive (>=) everywhere.

New features

  • setup_birdnet() installs and checks BirdNET. The BirdNET model is now downloaded by AudiomothR (with retries and an MD5 check) into the folder where the Python package ‘birdnet’ looks for it on Windows, macOS and Linux: its own download gave up after 30 s on slow connections. The messages of TensorFlow Lite are no longer shown.
  • One results folder per box, which gathers its successive SD cards: each card read is a deployment with its own dates, site and location (AudioMoth_<ID>_deployments.csv), so a box can be moved between sampling sites. BirdNET (location filter), the export to Observation.org (lat, lng, accuracy of each record), the validation and the report (map and table of the deployments) use the location of each card. The location is given with coordinates or taken from CONFIG.TXT with a warning, and is asked for in interactive sessions (Enter = the previous site). Only the new recordings are analysed, and the results of cards no longer connected are kept.
  • When output is not given, read_audiomoth() and process_audiomoth() ask for the results folder (choose_output()), suggesting one outside the card and remembering the folder of each box; in non-interactive sessions the remembered folder is used, or it must be given. Before, the results were saved inside the card.
  • The metadata of the WAV files are cached in the results folder (.inventory_cache.rds): reading a card again only reads the new or changed files.
  • create_validation() creates a self-contained web page to validate the records by ear before exporting them: one card per species and day, from the least to the most plausible (confidence and probability of occurrence at the site), with audio clips, spectrograms and the other species that BirdNET proposed. Records can be marked as valid, not valid or unsure, or relabelled with autocompletion. read_validation() reads the decisions (also from the Downloads folder) and export_observation() applies them: validated records are exported with is certain = True even with a single detection, and those marked as not valid are left out.
  • analyze_birdnet() stores the probability of occurrence of each species at the site and week (location_prob), the UTC offset of each detection and the versions of the software (birdnet/<ID>_<key>/metadata.txt).
  • Triggered recordings (*T.WAV, amplitude or frequency threshold) are expanded before the analysis, so that times and durations are right.
  • read_audiomoth() reads cards without CONFIG.TXT, GUANO metadata (exact battery voltage), comments with a deployment ID, and finds duplicated recordings.
  • process_audiomoth() gains precision_m, example_species = "auto", video, export, validation and checks its arguments before the analysis.
  • detected_species() returns the vector it prints, ready for extract_examples(), which also accepts a list of recorders.
  • parse_coordinates() reads hemisphere letters before the numbers or written in words, degrees-minutes-seconds without symbols, typographic minus signs, Google Maps links and named numeric vectors, and rejects texts that are not coordinates.

Bug fixes (audit of 2026-10-26)

  • Coordinates: the sign was lost with the hemisphere before the number, degrees-minutes-seconds separated by spaces gave wrong values, and swapped latitude and longitude were accepted without warning (now compared with CONFIG.TXT). The precision of a numeric vector was about 69 km.
  • Taxonomy: the BirdNET → IOC table was rebuilt from the BirdNET v2.4 labels and the official IOC comparison with other checklists (data-raw/build_taxonomy.R): the 250 birds that were lost (Eurasian jackdaw, cattle egret, little ringed plover, alpine swift, goshawk…) now reach Observation.org. Species split by IOC are translated according to the location (regional_rules.csv) or reported. Own equivalences are checked.
  • Observation.org: the exported names are now those of the species list of Observation.org (downloaded on 2026-10-28), which differs from IOC in some lumps and genera: every bird of BirdNET v2.4 has a valid name (e.g. Corvus cornix → Corvus corone, Saxicola stejnegeri → Saxicola maurus, Tumbezia salvini → Ochthoeca salvini), and the BirdNET name is kept in the notes when they differ.
  • BirdNET cache: changing a parameter no longer deletes previous results; arguments are checked before anything is written; interrupted conversions and results are written atomically and detected; errors are recorded in the column analysis and in errors.csv; an empty location filter or an analysis where every recording fails are errors instead of “0 detections”. The cache is separated by recorder. Doubts no longer depend on min_confidence and classes that are not species (“Engine”, “Human vocal”…) no longer count as species nor as doubts. Overlapping windows are grouped into events. BirdNET weeks follow the eBird convention. The Polish labels of BirdNET v2.4, which are wrong, are rejected.
  • Examples: successive calls add to the index instead of replacing it, the scroll video no longer overwrites the cursor one, paths are relative, a failed example does not stop the others, species names are matched without accents and by IOC name, 24 and 32-bit WAV files are read, and the scroll video is no longer quadratic in time.
  • Observation.org: the location of am is used (not that of the analysis), accuracy above 1000 m is warned about, from/to accept DD/MM/YYYY, the external reference is unique and stable, and a CSV edited by hand is not overwritten.
  • Report: it no longer deletes the examples, keeps the edits of its template, flags recorders not analysed, counts only analysed audio, survives missing temperature or dates, site names with quotes or @, CSV files saved with ;, and shows the real error of Quarto. Quarto receives .libPaths().
  • Inventory: faster, with the gain of each recording, the UTC offset of old firmware (Time zone), warnings about WAV files outside the daily folders, a clear error when the card is write-protected, time zones such as "UTC+2", and a warning when the time zone does not fit the location (Canary Islands).
  • The example data and tests no longer contain the ID or location of a real recorder.
  • Triggered recordings (T.WAV): the compressed blocks are aligned with the file, not with the start of the audio, and the expanded file is written in pieces. Links of Google Maps: the marked point is used, never the centre of the map view (@). Duplicated recordings name the copy that is kept. Thanks to José Antonio Barbero-Aparicio, whose review (pull request #1, on version 0.2.0) found these problems, provided the tests of T.WAV files and deployment IDs, and independently confirmed the BirdNET → IOC table.

AudiomothR 0.2.0

  • crear_informe(): PDF report (Quarto + Typst) of one or several recorders.
  • especies_detectadas(), number of examples per species and comprobar_requisitos().

AudiomothR 0.1.0

  • First version: reading AudioMoth cards, analysis with BirdNET, audio, spectrogram and video examples, and export to Observation.org.
